chapter: The cancelled dance and race in New Orleans
title: What happened that night and the crowd's reaction
summary: Alcorn describes the crowd going home crushed, the unknown cause and the poor people who had bought tickets.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Where did you all go after? After that thing?

Yeah. Everybody walked with the heels down. Came home with the sand. Looked like a fume. Looked like a blue head died or something, man. Because it couldn't end. Yeah. That's how the people was coming back, man. People came from all out in the country.
Who were the... You said it was the promoters? Did the law have anything to do with it?

I don't know what it was. We never found out that. I know they didn't have it that night. Uh-huh. I waited for some guys to tell you. But you had so many tears on it. Yeah. I'm just telling you it was a disappointment. Sure.

I wouldn't add on to it what it was. But they said it was... I know he was hurt because he wanted to play. And they was announcing that people was buying tickets and getting things together. Women was buying dresses to go to that that night. And that took the pressure, man.
People wanted to have a look. Yeah.
He was disappointed in himself. But money didn't mean nothing to him on that.
The boys would have gotten richer on it though.
